addedLines: - agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-py: Use this agent to verify that a Python Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a Python Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-ts: Use this agent to verify that a TypeScript Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plugin-dev:agent-creator: Use this agent when the user asks to "create an agent", "generate an agent", "build a new agent", "make me an agent that...", or describes agent functionality they need. Trigger when user wants to create autonomous agents for plugins. Examples:

<example>
Context: User wants to create a code review agent
user: "Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate the agent configuration."
<commentary>
User requesting new agent creation, trigger agent-creator to generate it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User describes needed functionality
user: "I need an agent that generates unit tests for my code"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to create a test generation agent."
<commentary>
User describes agent need, trigger agent-creator to build it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User wants to add agent to plugin
user: "Add an agent to my plugin that validates configurations"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate a configuration validator agent."
<commentary>
Plugin development with agent addition, trigger agent-creator.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Write, Read)

- plugin-dev:plugin-validator: Use this agent when the user asks to "validate my plugin", "check plugin structure", "verify plugin is correct", "validate plugin.json", "check plugin files", or mentions plugin validation. Also trigger proactively after user creates or modifies plugin components. Examples:

<example>

assistant: "Great! Let me validate the plugin structure."
<commentary>
Plugin created, proactively validate to catch issues early.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the plugin."
</example>

<example>
Context: User explicitly requests validation

assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to perform comprehensive validation."

Explicit validation request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

assistant: "Let me validate the changes."
<commentary>
Manifest modified, validate to ensure correctness.
</commentary>

</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to analyze the skill quality."

assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the changes."
<commentary>
Skill description modified, review for triggering effectiveness.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.

<example>

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. - Adds a dedicated `/preview?entry=<entryId>` route that loads the Contentful Live Preview SDK with inspector mode and live updates enabled — editors can use this as their preview URL in the Contentful web app
- Auto-detects the entry's Experience content type via `getEntry()` so the route works for any Experience type, not just `collectionPageExp`

- Existing `/:slug` experience route gains optional `?preview` query param support for slug-based preview links
- Adds `b2c-dx-mcp` MCP server to project scope in `.mcp.json`

## Preview URL format

Configure this in your Contentful space under **Settings → Content preview**:

```
https://<your-storefront-host>/preview?entry={entry.sys.id}
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Open the preview URL in the Contentful web app — experience renders without errors
- [ ] Inspector mode overlays appear on Contentful components when hovering in the preview panel
- [ ] Live edits in the Contentful editor reflect in the preview without a page refresh
- [ ] `/preview` without `?entry=` shows a clear error message
- [ ] `/:slug` route without `?preview` is unaffected

{"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjQ4NDI2NjU1","is_bot":false,"login":"mani060689","name":""},"baseRefName":"develop","body":"## Summary

- New workflow `sync-env-vars-to-mrt.yml` — triggered manually from GitHub Actions → Run workflow
- No hardcoded variable names: reads `.env.sample` for the key list, fetches actual values from the selected GitHub Environment via the GitHub API, then intersects the two
- Only keys that are **set and non-empty** in the GitHub Environment are PATCHed to MRT — missing keys are silently skipped so MRT retains existing values
- `scope:personal` and `scope:auto` keys (including `ENVIRONMENT_NAME`) are never synced
- Supports **dry run** mode — shows exactly what would be synced without touching MRT

## How it works

```
.env.sample  →  parse scope:shared + scope:tier keys
                        ↓
GitHub API   →  GET /environments/{target}/variables  (all set vars)
                        ↓
intersection →  keys in both + non-empty value
                        ↓
MRT API      →  PATCH /projects/zimmermann/target/{target}/env-var/
```

## Usage

**GitHub Actions → Workflows → "Sync Env Vars to MRT" → Run workflow**

Select target (`dev` / `test` / `sit` / `uat` / `staging` / `prod`) and optionally enable dry run.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run with `dry_run: true` for `dev` — verify output lists the expected keys without calling MRT
- [ ] Run with `dry_run: false` for `dev` — verify MRT target shows updated values in Runtime Admin
- [ ] Add a new key to `.env.sample` — verify it appears in the next sync without any workflow change
- [ ] Leave a key unset in the GitHub Environment — verify it is skipped in the sync log

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Chores**
  - Added a manually triggered **“Sync Env Vars to MRT”** GitHub Actions workflow to sync selected configuration keys from the repository’s environment sample to the chosen deployment target.

- **Documentation**
  - Updated the README with workflow usage, required secrets, and guidance on when to run it after updating a GitHub Environment.

+name: Sync Env Vars to MRT
+
+# Reads all scope:shared and scope:tier keys from .env.sample, fetches their
+# values from the selected GitHub Environment via the GitHub API, then PATCHes
+# only the keys that are actually set (non-empty) to the MRT target.
+#
+# Keys that exist in .env.sample but have no value in the GitHub Environment
+# are silently skipped — MRT retains whatever value it already holds for them.
+#
+# scope:personal and scope:auto keys (including ENVIRONMENT_NAME) are never
+# synced — they are developer-local or script-injected.
+#
+# Trigger: manual only (workflow_dispatch). Run after updating a GitHub
+# Environment to propagate new values to MRT without a full redeploy.
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      target:
+        description: 'MRT target to update'
+        required: true
+        type: choice
+        options:
+          - dev
+          - test
+          - sit
+          - uat
+          - staging
+          - prod
+      dry_run:
+        description: 'Dry run — show what would be synced without calling MRT'
+        required: false
+        type: boolean
+        default: false
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  sync:
+    name: Sync to MRT (${{ inputs.target }})
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment: ${{ inputs.target }}
+    env:
+      MRT_USER: ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
+      MRT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
+      MRT_PROJECT: zimmermann
+      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_ENV_READ_TOKEN }}
+      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+
+      - name: Set up Python
+        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: '3.12'
+
+      - name: Parse syncable keys from .env.sample
+        id: parse
+        run: |
+          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
+          import re, os, json
+
+          SKIP_KEYS   = {'ENVIRONMENT_NAME'}          # scope:auto — MRT sets this itself
+          SKIP_SCOPES = {'personal', 'auto'}
+
+          keys = []
+          pending_scope = None
+          with open('.env.sample') as f:
+              for line in f:
+                  line = line.rstrip('\n')
+                  m = re.match(r'^#\s*scope:(\w+)', line)
+                  if m:
+                      pending_scope = m.group(1)
+                      continue
+                  stripped = line.strip()
+                  if not stripped or stripped.startswith('#'):
+                      pending_scope = None
+                      continue
+                  eq = stripped.find('=')
+                  if eq == -1:
+                      pending_scope = None
+                      continue
+                  key = stripped[:eq].strip()
+                  scope = pending_scope
+                  pending_scope = None
+                  if not scope or scope in SKIP_SCOPES or key in SKIP_KEYS:
+                      continue
+                  keys.append(key)
+
+          print(f'Parsed {len(keys)} syncable keys from .env.sample')
+          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
+              out.write(f'keys={json.dumps(keys)}\n')
+          PYEOF
+
+      - name: Fetch GitHub Environment variables
+        id: gh_vars
+        run: |
+          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
+          import json, os, subprocess, sys
+
+          TARGET = os.environ['TARGET']
+          REPO   = os.environ['GH_REPO']
+
+          # GitHub Environment variables are readable via the API (plain-text by design —
+          # see .env.sample header note). --paginate returns all pages in one call.
+          all_vars = {}
+          result = subprocess.run(
+              ['gh', 'api', f'/repos/{REPO}/environments/{TARGET}/variables',
+               '--paginate', '--jq', '.variables[] | {(.name): .value}'],
+              capture_output=True, text=True
+          )
+          if result.returncode != 0:
+              print(f'GitHub API error: {result.stderr}', file=sys.stderr)
+              sys.exit(1)
+          # gh --jq outputs one JSON object per line when iterating
+          for line in result.stdout.strip().splitlines():
+              if line:
+                  all_vars.update(json.loads(line))
+
+          print(f'Found {len(all_vars)} variables set in GitHub Environment: {TARGET}')
+          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
+              out.write(f'vars={json.dumps(all_vars)}\n')
+          PYEOF
+        env:
+          TARGET: ${{ inputs.target }}
+
+      - name: Build payload and sync to MRT
+        run: |
+          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
+          import base64, json, os, sys, urllib.request, urllib.error
+
+          DRY_RUN = os.environ.get('DRY_RUN', 'false').lower() == 'true'
+          TARGET  = os.environ['TARGET']
+          PROJECT = os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
+          USER    = os.environ['MRT_USER']
+          API_KEY = os.environ['MRT_API_KEY']
+
+          syncable_keys = json.loads(os.environ['SYNC_KEYS'])
+          gh_vars       = json.loads(os.environ['GH_VARS'])
+
+          # Intersect: only keys in .env.sample that have a value in GitHub
+          payload = {}
+          skipped_empty = []
+          skipped_missing = []
+          for key in syncable_keys:
+              if key in gh_vars:
+                  val = gh_vars[key]
+                  if val:
+                      payload[key] = val
+                  else:
+                      skipped_empty.append(key)
+              else:
+                  skipped_missing.append(key)
+
+          print(f'Keys to sync:    {len(payload)}')
+          print(f'Skipped (empty): {len(skipped_empty)}')
+          print(f'Skipped (not in GitHub Environment): {len(skipped_missing)}')
+          if skipped_missing:
+              print('  Not set:', ', '.join(skipped_missing[:20]),
+                    '...' if len(skipped_missing) > 20 else '')
+
+          if not payload:
+              print('Nothing to sync.')
+              sys.exit(0)
+
+          if DRY_RUN:
+              print(f'\nDRY RUN — would PATCH {len(payload)} keys to MRT target: {TARGET}')
+              for k in sorted(payload):
+                  print(f'  {k}')
+              sys.exit(0)
+
+          token = base64.b64encode(f'{USER}:{API_KEY}'.encode()).decode()
+          url   = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/target/{TARGET}/env-var/'
+          req   = urllib.request.Request(
+              url,
+              data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
+              method='PATCH',
+              headers={
+                  'Authorization': f'Basic {token}',
+                  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
+              },
+          )
+          try:
+              resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
+              print(f'\nMRT response: {resp.status} {resp.reason}')
+              print(f'Synced {len(payload)} env vars to MRT target: {TARGET}')
+          except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
+              print(f'MRT API error {e.code}: {e.read().decode()}', file=sys.stderr)
+              sys.exit(1)
+          except TimeoutError:
+              print('MRT API request timed out after 30 s', file=sys.stderr)
+              sys.exit(1)
+          PYEOF
+        env:
+          TARGET: ${{ inputs.target }}
+          DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry_run }}
+          SYNC_KEYS: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.keys }}
+          GH_VARS: ${{ steps.gh_vars.outputs.vars }}

content.text:
## Bottom line

Neither PR #41 nor #42 introduced the "products not displaying" failure. The product breakage is a **back-end SCAPI hook error on the `bkzk_002` dev instance**, which is exactly the "pending build/integration" class you told me to set aside — not a regression in mani's front-end/CI deploys.

Here's the evidence chain.

## Why the product 500s are back-end, not front-end

The two calls that break product display both fail the same way:

```
product-search?...refine=cgid=clothing   → 500   sfdc_customization: HOOK
products/Test?...                         → 500   sfdc_customization: HOOK
body: {"title":"Internal Server Error", "type":".../internal-server-error"}
```

- **`sfdc_customization: HOOK`** is the definitive tell: a server-side B2C Commerce SCAPI hook (a `beforeGET`/`modifyGETResponse` script registered in a cartridge on the SFCC instance) ran and threw. That's the *back end* returning 500 to the PWA — the PWA is just the client receiving it. Nothing in this repo deploys SCAPI hooks.
- Contrast the `shopper-context` call, which is **404 with no `sfdc_customization` header** — that's the platform saying "no guest context set," which is normal, not a hook failure.
- Both a **stock base request** (the PLP) and a **customised request** (the home scroller) fail identically → the common factor is the back-end hook, not any request parameter.

## Why PR #41 and #42 can't be the cause

**PR #42** (`sync-env-vars-to-mrt`) — a `workflow_dispatch` GitHub Action + README only. It has zero runtime footprint on localhost, and even its worst case (running it with bad GitHub Environment values) only PATCHes **MRT** env vars for the Node PWA server — it can't produce a SCAPI `HOOK` 500 on the SFCC instance, and localhost reads local `config/` + `.env`, not MRT. Fully exonerated.

**PR #41** (`storefront-preview-contentful`) — touches only Contentful/routing:
- Route ordering is safe. `..._routes` (base SFCC routes incl. `/category/:categoryId`, `/product/:productId`, `/search`) is spread **before** the new `/preview` (which is `exact`) and the `/:slug` Experience catch-all, so the catch-all never intercepts PLP/PDP.
- It doesn't touch any product data path. On this branch there is **no `product-list`/`product-detail` override at all** — those are base `retail-react-app`, and the failing PLP request's params (`page_meta_tags`, `custom_properties`, `perPricebook=true`, `allVariationProperties=true`) are **base v10 defaults** (`node_modules/.../product-list/index.jsx:169-178`), not a customisation.
- Its new pages are `loadable` (lazy) and Contentful-only, so they can't crash PLP/PDP even if they errored.

(One pre-existing nit I noticed while reading it: `experience/index.tsx` calls `useFetchBySlug` after an early `if (!client) return` — a Rules-of-Hooks smell — but that pattern predates PR #41 and only affects Experience slug pages, not products.)

## The noise to ignore (pending integrations / expected-in-dev)

All unrelated to mani's PRs:

- **Einstein** `Failed to fetch` / `POST .../v3/activities//viewProduct` — note the empty `//` segment: the Einstein site/client ID isn't configured, so the URLs are malformed. Config gap.
- **Data Cloud** `ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED` on `*.c360a.salesforce.com` — not provisioned.
- **Contentful** `unknownContentType "DOESNOTEXIST"` — content model not synced yet.
- `Missing translation "header.button.assistive_msg.search"`, and the webpack `GithubLogo`/`FigmaLogo` "not found" warnings (base home data referencing icons the Zimmermann icons override removed) — cosmetic.
- `viewBox did not match` (Server `0 0 631 74` vs Client `0 0 46 32`) and `getServerSnapshot should be cached` — pre-existing app-shell hydration warnings, present regardless of #41/#42.

**Important:** the scary-looking `useActiveData … reading 'map'` and `use-einstein … reading 'id'` crashes are **downstream of the 500** — product-search returns no `hits`, so the tracking code maps over `undefined`. Fix the back-end hook and these secondary errors go away too.

## What to do next

Escalate the SCAPI hook failure to whoever owns the cartridges/hooks on the `bkzk_002` dev instance (Integration/SI partner). Ask them to check what changed on the **SFCC side** around when products stopped rendering — a `shopper-search`/`shopper-products` `beforeGET`/`modifyGETResponse` hook is throwing. Give them these correlation IDs to pull the exact stack in Log Center:

- product-search 500 → `sfdc_correlation_id: a2203b658c3306e4`
- products/Test 500 → `sfdc_correlation_id: a2203b831c37b929`

If mani's "temporary deploy" was a *cartridge/hook* push to the dev instance (separate from PRs #41/#42), that's the thing to revert — not the PWA PRs.

Want me to (a) draft that escalation note for SFCC-29, or (b) pull the Jira comment to cross-check what was reported (I'd need Atlassian MCP access enabled — it's in `.mcp.json` but not exposed to me here)?

The principle is simple: **isolate the variable.** The back end is fixed (`qmyt7hks` / `f_ecom_bkzk_002` / `ZimmermannAU`). If we remove React from the loop — or swap the front end for a different version — and the 500 still happens, the front end is excluded by construction. Here's how to prove it, plus the evidence that already points that way.

## The decisive test: replay the request with no React

Grab a **fresh** Bearer token (DevTools → Network → click any `…commercecloud.salesforce.com` request → copy the `authorization` request header — the one in your log expired 30 min after mint), then hit SCAPI *directly*, bypassing the PWA entirely:

```bash
TOKEN='Bearer eyJ...'   # fresh token from DevTools

# 1) The exact call the PLP makes — but straight to SCAPI, zero PWA:
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -H "authorization: $TOKEN" \
 'https://qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com/search/shopper-search/v1/organizations/f_ecom_bkzk_002/product-search?siteId=ZimmermannAU&refine=cgid%3Dclothing&currency=AUD&locale=en&limit=25'

# 2) Minimal call — drop every param the FE adds (expand, custom_properties,
#    allVariationProperties, perPricebook). If THIS still 500s, no FE input matters:
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -H "authorization: $TOKEN" \
 'https://qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com/search/shopper-search/v1/organizations/f_ecom_bkzk_002/product-search?siteId=ZimmermannAU&q=dress&currency=AUD&locale=en&limit=5'
```

If either returns `500` + `sfdc_customization: HOOK`, there is no React, no PWA proxy, no override code in the path — so the cause cannot be front end. **Paste me a fresh token and I'll run both for you.**

## Bisect the front end (holds the back end constant)

Swap only the front-end version against the same back end:

- Check out `develop` (pre-#41/#42) or the last-known-good commit, load the same PLP. Same 500 → front-end code excluded by bisection.
- Or point the **pristine base `retail-react-app`** at the same org/site — no Zimmermann overrides at all. Same 500 → confirmed.

I can do the `git checkout` to stage this; you'd load the page (I won't start the dev server per project rules).

## Evidence already in hand (no repro needed)

**1. The PWA proxy is a transparent forwarder — it can't manufacture this error.** `config/default.js:208-215`:
```js
proxyConfigs: [
  { host: 'qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com', path: 'api' },
  { host: 'bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com',  path: 'ocapi' },
]
```
`/mobify/proxy/api/*` → `https://qmyt7hks…/*`, verbatim. The Node layer rewrites the URL and forwards; it does not add params, run hooks, or emit `application/problem+json`.

**2. Front-end auth succeeded — the failure is downstream of it.** The token on the failing request decodes to a valid guest session:
```json
{"sub":"cc-slas::bkzk_002::…usid:59b4364e…", "ssc":"qmyt7hks",
 "aud":"commercecloud/production/bkzk-002-…", "chid":"ZimmermannAU",
 "scp":"sfcc.shopper-standard …"}
```
Correct org, correct site, valid guest scopes. SLAS (the FE's job) worked. The 500 happens *after* auth, inside the hook.

**3. The response is Salesforce-stamped.** `application/problem+json`, `x-proxy-request-url`, `sfdc_correlation_id`, `cf-ray` (Cloudflare), `x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 63`, `sfdc_customization: HOOK`, `sfdc_cache_status: MISS` — all generated at the SF edge/origin. A front-end/proxy fault yields a connection error or a PWA-shaped error, never these.

**4. Negative controls in the same session are healthy.** The SLAS token mint succeeded, and `shopper-context` returned a clean **404 with no HOOK header** — so transport, auth, and proxy all work. Only the two hook-decorated endpoints (`shopper-search`, `shopper-products`) 500. The fault is localized to the hook, not the pipe.

## The definitive back-end proof (needs SFCC access)

Pull SFCC **Log Center → Request/Custom log** by correlation ID — `a2203b658c3306e4` (product-search) and `a2203b831c37b929` (products/Test). A hook script stack trace there names the exact cartridge, hook, and line. That's incontrovertible; the Integration/SI partner can retrieve it.

## What a front-end cause would have looked like (and didn't)

Every front-end signature is absent: no JS/render error *before* the fetch; no malformed URL (contrast the real Einstein bug — `…/activities//viewProduct`, empty segment); no 4xx from bad params or auth; no CORS/connection error; and the params in the failing request are **base v10 defaults**, not override code. Instead: well-formed request → valid auth → correct upstream URL → server-generated 500 from a hook. That is a back-end signature, top to bottom.

This overturns part of my earlier claim, and I need to own that directly: I predicted the stripped-down request would also 500 — it did **not**. C1, C2 and E all returned **200 with real product data**. That's a more useful result than I expected, and it sharpens the diagnosis rather than weakening it.

## What the results actually prove

| Test | Params | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **A** proxy, full params | expand + perPricebook + allVariationProperties + sort + allImages | **500** + HOOK |
| **B** direct SCAPI, full params | same | **500** + HOOK |
| **C1** direct, category, no expand | `refine=cgid=clothing&limit=5` | **200** ✅ (product `4673TS251`) |
| **C2** direct, text search, no expand | `q=dress` | **200** ✅ (product `8637DS241`) |
| **D** shopper-context | — | **404**, no HOOK ✅ control |
| **E** PDP, reduced expand | `expand=availability,prices,images,variations` | **200** ✅ |

Three things are now nailed down:

1. **The 500 is generated server-side, not by the PWA.** Test B has zero PWA in the path (curl → SCAPI) and still 500s. So React, React-Query, and the Node proxy are all exonerated — that part of my earlier answer holds.
2. **It is parameter-triggered, not unconditional.** A minimal query succeeds; the fuller query crashes. So the hook doesn't fail on every request — it throws on a specific input the storefront adds. (Note `sfdc_customization: HOOK` shows on the **200s too** — the hook *runs* on every search; only certain params make it *throw*.)
3. **Only one product in `cgid=clothing` (`"total":1`)** — the dev catalog/search index is barely populated. Separate pending-data issue, but relevant: the hook is crashing while *expanding that handful of products*.

## Refined verdict

Still not PR #41 or #42 — they don't touch product-search params at all. And the params that trigger it (`expand=…page_meta_tags,custom_properties`, `perPricebook=true`, `allVariationProperties=true`) are **base retail-react-app v10 defaults** (`product-list/index.jsx:169-178`), not anything mani or the FE team added.

So the accurate framing is: **a back-end SCAPI hook crashes when it processes the standard expand/pricing parameters the storefront sends by default.** That's a back-end defect on valid input — the fix belongs in the hook — but it only surfaces for the real PLP/PDP query shape, which is why a naive "is the backend up?" check would look fine. My "even the minimal request 500s" claim was wrong; the value is that we can now point the back-end team at the *exact* parameter.

## Next: pinpoint the trigger (one paste)

This adds one parameter at a time onto the known-good baseline and prints just the status code, so we find the exact flip from 200→500:

```bash
hit () { printf '%-34s ' "$2"; curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' -H "authorization: $TOKEN" "$1"; }
B="$SCAPI/search/shopper-search/v1/organizations/$ORG/product-search?siteId=$SITE&refine=cgid%3Dclothing&currency=AUD&locale=en&limit=25"

hit "$B"                                                                          "baseline (200 expected)"
hit "$B&sort=best-matches"                                                        "+sort"
hit "$B&allImages=true"                                                           "+allImages"
hit "$B&perPricebook=true"                                                        "+perPricebook"
hit "$B&allVariationProperties=true"                                             "+allVariationProperties"
hit "$B&expand=promotions%2Cvariations%2Cprices%2Cimages%2Cpage_meta_tags%2Ccustom_properties" "+full expand"
hit "$B&expand=promotions"                                                        "+expand=promotions"
hit "$B&expand=prices"                                                            "+expand=prices"
hit "$B&expand=page_meta_tags"                                                    "+expand=page_meta_tags"
hit "$B&expand=custom_properties"                                                 "+expand=custom_properties"
hit "$B&expand=variations"                                                        "+expand=variations"
hit "$B&expand=images"                                                            "+expand=images"
hit "$B&perPricebook=true&expand=prices"                                          "+perPricebook+expand=prices"
hit "$B&expand=prices%2Cpromotions"                                               "+expand=prices,promotions"
hit "$B&allVariationProperties=true&expand=variations"                            "+allVarProps+expand=variations"
```

Reading it:
- **First single param that flips to `HTTP 500`** = the input the hook chokes on. `perPricebook`/`expand=prices`/`expand=promotions` would point at a **pricing or promotions hook** (very plausible here given Global-e); `expand=custom_properties` points at a custom-attribute hook; `expand=page_meta_tags` at an SEO/meta hook.
- **If every single param passes but `+full expand` fails**, it's a *combination* — paste the results and I'll give you the pairwise second pass.

Once we have the culprit param, the back-end team gets an exact repro (e.g. "`shopper-search` with `expand=prices&perPricebook=true` throws for product `4673TS251`"), and we can weigh a temporary storefront mitigation (drop that one expand) against the proper hook fix. Paste the block's output.

content.text:
That's the whole case closed — and it's now pinpointed. **Confirmed: not front end.** But the results also tell us *exactly* what trips it, which is more useful than "it's a backend hook."

## What the results prove

| Test | Result | What it establishes |
|---|---|---|
| **A** proxy, full params | 500 + HOOK | reproduces the browser |
| **B** direct SCAPI, full params | **500 + HOOK** | no PWA in the path at all → **not React, not the proxy** |
| **C1** direct, minimal (`refine=cgid=clothing`) | **200**, returns *Illuminate Fitted Blouse* | same backend, same token → catalog/index/pricebook/hook happy-path all work |
| **C2** direct, minimal (`q=dress`) | **200**, returns *Natura Mini Dress* | ditto |
| **D** control | clean 404, no HOOK | token + transport healthy |
| **E** PDP `products/Test` (no `page_meta_tags`) | **200** | PDP works once the heavy expands are dropped |

The decisive part isn't just that B failed — it's that **B failed and C1/C2 succeeded against the identical backend with the identical token.** The only thing that changed is the query parameters. So the failure is a **backend response hook that throws on a specific `expand` value the storefront requests** — 100% server-side, zero PWA (and therefore nothing to do with PR #41/#42, which don't touch these params anyway — they're base `retail-react-app` defaults).

## The prime suspect: `page_meta_tags`

Look at the delta between pass and fail:

- **Both failing calls** (PLP 500, and the original PDP 500 from your logs) requested `expand=…,page_meta_tags,…`
- **Every passing call** (C1, C2, and E) omitted `page_meta_tags`

That's the SEO meta-tag expansion hook — exactly the kind of custom `modifyGETResponse` hook that throws if it hits a null category/attribute. Let me confirm with a one-param-at-a-time bisection. Run this in the **same terminal** (your vars are still set; if you get `401`, the token lapsed — re-grab and re-paste the setup line):

```bash
BASE="$SCAPI/search/shopper-search/v1/organizations/$ORG/product-search?siteId=$SITE&refine=cgid%3Dclothing&currency=AUD&locale=en&limit=5"

for extra in \
  "" \
  "&expand=page_meta_tags" \
  "&expand=custom_properties" \
  "&expand=prices&perPricebook=true" \
  "&expand=variations&allVariationProperties=true" \
  "&allImages=true" \
  "&sort=best-matches" \
  "&expand=promotions%2Cvariations%2Cprices%2Cimages%2Ccustom_properties&allImages=true&perPricebook=true&allVariationProperties=true&sort=best-matches" \
  "&expand=promotions%2Cvariations%2Cprices%2Cimages%2Cpage_meta_tags%2Ccustom_properties&allImages=true&perPricebook=true&allVariationProperties=true&sort=best-matches" ; do
  code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "authorization: $TOKEN" "$BASE$extra")
  printf '%s   <- %s\n' "$code" "${extra:-<baseline, no extra params>}"
done
```

How to read it:
- Baseline → `200`. The first line that flips to `500` names the culprit.
- The last two lines are a leave-one-out check: entry 8 is the full PLP request **minus** `page_meta_tags`, entry 9 is the full PLP request **with** it. If 8 = `200` and 9 = `500`, that's proof it's `page_meta_tags`.

Then grab a correlation ID tied to just that param, for the SFCC team to pull the hook's stack in Log Center:

```bash
curl -sS -i -H "authorization: $TOKEN" \
"$SCAPI/search/shopper-search/v1/organizations/$ORG/product-search?siteId=$SITE&refine=cgid%3Dclothing&currency=AUD&locale=en&limit=5&expand=page_meta_tags" \
| grep -Ei 'HTTP/|sfdc_correlation_id'
```

## Where this lands

Ownership is **back end / Integration** — a SCAPI response hook (a `page_meta_tags` SEO-meta hook, most likely) on the `bkzk_002` dev instance is throwing on a valid, always-sent expand. That's the "pending build/integration" bucket; whatever backend change went out around the same time as mani's deploys is the thing to look at, not the PWA PRs.

A front-end "fix" (dropping `page_meta_tags` from the PLP/PDP expand) is possible but I'd **advise against it** except as a last-resort unblock: it means overriding two Tier-2 base pages and it would strip SEO meta tags — a real regression on an SEO-critical storefront per AGENTS.md. The right fix is the hook.

Run the bisection and paste the codes — once we've nailed the exact param I can write it up for SFCC-29 (with the correlation IDs) and, if useful, record the finding in project memory so the next person who sees "products not displaying" starts here instead of from scratch.

content.text:
Good news: the isolation is even cleaner than expected, but it also corrects my earlier guess — **it's not `page_meta_tags`, it's `allImages=true`.**

## Reading the bisection

| Param added to a passing baseline | Result |
|---|---|
| (nothing — baseline) | 200 |
| `expand=page_meta_tags` | 200 |
| `expand=custom_properties` | 200 |
| `expand=prices&perPricebook=true` | 200 |
| `expand=variations&allVariationProperties=true` | 200 |
| **`allImages=true`** | **500** |
| `sort=best-matches` | 200 |
| full kitchen-sink *with* `allImages=true` (×2 variants) | 500 |

One param, added alone to an otherwise-passing call, flips it from 200 to 500. That's about as clean a culprit isolation as this kind of testing gets.

**One correction to my own read of the data:** notice `sfdc_customization: HOOK` is present on the *successful* 200s too (C1, C2, E all have it). So that header isn't itself a failure signal — it just means "a custom hook is registered on this resource," success or fail. The actual signal is the status code. Good to know before we hand this to the backend team, so we don't misdescribe the symptom.

## One loose end: PDP isn't actually confirmed yet

Test E returned 200 for `products/Test` *with* `allImages=true` — but look closely, it used a **smaller** expand list than the PDP call that failed in your original browser log:

- Original failing PDP call: `expand=availability,promotions,options,images,prices,variations,set_products,bundled_products,page_meta_tags` + `allImages=true`
- Test E: `expand=availability,prices,images,variations` + `allImages=true` (missing `promotions`, `options`, `set_products`, `bundled_products`, `page_meta_tags`)

So Test E passing doesn't mean PDP is fine — it means we tested a different, smaller request. The real PDP trigger is still unisolated. Run this to pin it down the same way, using a real product ID from your C1/C2 results (`4673TS251`) instead of `Test`:

```bash
PBASE="$SCAPI/product/shopper-products/v1/organizations/$ORG/products/4673TS251?siteId=$SITE&currency=AUD&locale=en&allImages=true&perPricebook=true"

for extra in \
  "&expand=availability%2Cprices%2Cimages%2Cvariations" \
  "&expand=availability%2Cprices%2Cimages%2Cvariations%2Cpromotions" \
  "&expand=availability%2Cprices%2Cimages%2Cvariations%2Coptions" \
  "&expand=availability%2Cprices%2Cimages%2Cvariations%2Cset_products" \
  "&expand=availability%2Cprices%2Cimages%2Cvariations%2Cbundled_products" \
  "&expand=availability%2Cprices%2Cimages%2Cvariations%2Cpage_meta_tags" \
  "&expand=availability%2Cpromotions%2Coptions%2Cimages%2Cprices%2Cvariations%2Cset_products%2Cbundled_products%2Cpage_meta_tags" ; do
  code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "authorization: $TOKEN" "$PBASE$extra")
  printf '%s   <- %s\n' "$code" "$extra"
done
```

The last line reproduces the exact original failing request (as a sanity check that we're testing the right thing) — the ones above it isolate which single `expand` value is responsible.

Also worth closing the loop on necessity for PLP (proves `allImages=true` isn't just sufficient but also the *only* thing wrong with the full param set):

```bash
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "authorization: $TOKEN" \
"$SCAPI/search/shopper-search/v1/organizations/$ORG/product-search?siteId=$SITE&refine=cgid%3Dclothing&sort=best-matches&currency=AUD&locale=en&expand=promotions%2Cvariations%2Cprices%2Cimages%2Cpage_meta_tags%2Ccustom_properties&perPricebook=true&allVariationProperties=true&limit=25&offset=0"
```
(identical to the original failing PLP request, minus `allImages=true` — expect `200`)

I'm logging what we've confirmed so far to project memory now, so if this comes up again before it's fixed upstream, we don't re-run the whole investigation from scratch.

`shopper-search` (product-search) and `shopper-products` calls to the
`bkzk_002` SCAPI instance return `500 Internal Server Error` with an
`sfdc_customization: HOOK` response header — a custom SCAPI hook on the
Salesforce side is throwing, not the PWA.

bypassing the PWA dev server and its `/mobify/proxy` layer entirely — using a
captured guest bearer token; identical 500 + HOOK with zero PWA in the path.

(`overrides/app/pages/` only has `experience`, `home`, `my-new-route` on this
branch) — the failing requests use `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10's stock
default parameters, not a Zimmermann customization. Ruled out mani's
concurrent PRs #41 (`feature/storefront-preview-contentful`) and #42
(`feature/sync-env-vars-to-mrt`) as the cause — neither touches
product-search/product-detail request parameters at all; #42 is CI-only.

**PLP root cause pinpointed via query-param bisection** (direct-to-SCAPI, one
param added at a time on top of a passing baseline
`product-search?refine=cgid=clothing&currency=AUD&locale=en&limit=5` → 200):
adding only `allImages=true` flips the same call to 500. Every other param
tested individually (`expand=page_meta_tags`, `expand=custom_properties`,
`expand=prices&perPricebook=true`, `expand=variations&allVariationProperties=true`,
`sort=best-matches`) stayed 200. Note `sfdc_customization: HOOK` appears on
*successful* hooked-endpoint responses too — it marks "a custom hook is
registered on this resource," not failure by itself; the status code is the
real signal, not that header.

**PDP (`shopper-products`) trigger not yet isolated as of 2026-07-28.** A
reduced-param direct call to `products/Test` with `allImages=true` returned
200 — that does NOT mean PDP is fine, it means a smaller param set was
tested. The original failing browser request additionally carried
`expand=promotions,options,set_products,bundled_products,page_meta_tags`,
none of which were in the passing reduced call. Needs its own bisection
round (same method as PLP) before assuming the same `allImages=true` cause.

Why: took a full session of curl-based isolation to separate from unrelated
"pending build/integration" noise in the same console log (Einstein
`Failed to fetch`, Data Cloud `ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`, Contentful
`unknownContentType`) — all separately broken/unconfigured in dev but
unrelated to this outage — and from an initial wrong guess (`page_meta_tags`)
that the bisection data corrected.

How to apply: if "products not displaying in dev" comes up again before this
is fixed upstream, don't re-run the frontend-vs-backend investigation from
scratch — it's confirmed backend, owned by Integration/SI partner, on the
`bkzk_002` SCAPI hook. Point them at: baseline + `allImages=true` on
product-search reproduces cleanly and gives a correlation ID for Log Center.
Do not attempt a frontend workaround (e.g. stripping `allImages` from a new
product-list override) without explicit user approval — `allImages` controls
per-variant image completeness, likely an intentional data requirement, and
`product-list` has no override yet so adding one is a Copy-first-rule task,
not a quick patch.

content.text:
Two important things happened in that batch — one closes PLP for good, the other flips my read of PDP.

## PLP: closed, fully proven

The necessity check came back **200**. So we now have both directions nailed down on the *entire* 25-product clothing category, not just one item:

- full PLP params **with** `allImages=true` → 500
- identical params **without** it → 200

`allImages=true` is proven **necessary and sufficient** to break `product-search`. Nothing else to test here.

## PDP: the real signal isn't the expand param — it's the product

Look again at what happened. **Every single expand variation 500'd** — including the exact same minimal shape (`expand=availability,prices,images,variations` + `allImages=true` + `perPricebook=true`) that returned **200** last round on `products/Test`. The only thing that changed between a passing call and a failing one was **the product ID** (`Test` → `4673TS251`).

That's a cleaner isolation than any expand-param bisection could give us: same query, one variable changed, flips 200→500. So the PDP trigger isn't "which expand values you ask for" — it's something about *this specific product's* data (most likely its variant/image records) hitting a hook bug that a near-empty stub product like `Test` never exercises.

What we don't yet know: is this the **same root cause as PLP** (i.e., `allImages=true` + a product that actually has real variant/image data to iterate — `Test` has nothing to iterate, so it slips through regardless of the flag), or a **separate PDP-only bug** that doesn't care about `allImages` at all? One test tells us which:

```bash
# Same real product, same everything, minus allImages — isolates whether allImages is still the trigger
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "authorization: $TOKEN" \
"$SCAPI/product/shopper-products/v1/organizations/$ORG/products/4673TS251?siteId=$SITE&currency=AUD&locale=en&perPricebook=true&expand=availability%2Cprices%2Cimages%2Cvariations"

# Bare product fetch, zero expand, zero allImages — does merely fetching this product break?
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "authorization: $TOKEN" \
"$SCAPI/product/shopper-products/v1/organizations/$ORG/products/4673TS251?siteId=$SITE&currency=AUD&locale=en"

# Bare + allImages=true only, still zero expand — isolates allImages in total isolation
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "authorization: $TOKEN" \
"$SCAPI/product/shopper-products/v1/organizations/$ORG/products/4673TS251?siteId=$SITE&currency=AUD&locale=en&allImages=true"
```

Reading the three results:
- **Line 1 → 200**: confirms unified cause — same bug as PLP, `allImages=true` + a product with real variant/image data. One root cause, two endpoints.
- **Line 1 → 500**: it's not about `allImages` at all for PDP; something else about this product trips it regardless. Check lines 2 and 3 next — if line 2 (fully bare) already 500s, the bug fires on *any* request for this product's data, meaning it's likely a corrupt/unusual field on this specific SKU, not a request-shape issue.
- **Line 3 → 500 but line 2 → 200**: confirms `allImages=true` alone (zero other params) is enough on this product — the cleanest possible PDP isolation.

I've updated the memory record to reflect the sharper finding (product-identity is a confirmed factor, not just param shape) — pending this last test to know whether it's the same `allImages` cause or a second bug.

SFCC-29 (dev environment): PLP and PDP fail to display products because
`shopper-search` (product-search) and `shopper-products` calls to the
`bkzk_002` SCAPI instance return `500 Internal Server Error` with an
`sfdc_customization: HOOK` response header — a custom SCAPI hook on the
Salesforce side is throwing, not the PWA.

**Confirmed not frontend.** Reproduced by hitting SCAPI directly with curl —
bypassing the PWA dev server and its `/mobify/proxy` layer entirely — using a
captured guest bearer token; identical 500 + HOOK with zero PWA in the path.
No override exists for `product-list`/`product-detail` in this repo
(`overrides/app/pages/` only has `experience`, `home`, `my-new-route` on this
branch) — the failing requests use `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10's stock
default parameters, not a Zimmermann customization. Ruled out mani's
concurrent PRs #41 (`feature/storefront-preview-contentful`) and #42
(`feature/sync-env-vars-to-mrt`) as the cause — neither touches
product-search/product-detail request parameters at all; #42 is CI-only.

**PLP root cause pinpointed via query-param bisection** (direct-to-SCAPI, one
param added at a time on top of a passing baseline
`product-search?refine=cgid=clothing&currency=AUD&locale=en&limit=5` → 200):
adding only `allImages=true` flips the same call to 500. Every other param
tested individually (`expand=page_meta_tags`, `expand=custom_properties`,
`expand=prices&perPricebook=true`, `expand=variations&allVariationProperties=true`,
`sort=best-matches`) stayed 200. Note `sfdc_customization: HOOK` appears on
*successful* hooked-endpoint responses too — it marks "a custom hook is
registered on this resource," not failure by itself; the status code is the
real signal, not that header.

**PDP (`shopper-products`) trigger not yet isolated as of 2026-07-28.** A
reduced-param direct call to `products/Test` with `allImages=true` returned
200 — that does NOT mean PDP is fine, it means a smaller param set was
tested. The original failing browser request additionally carried
`expand=promotions,options,set_products,bundled_products,page_meta_tags`,
none of which were in the passing reduced call. Needs its own bisection
round (same method as PLP) before assuming the same `allImages=true` cause.

Why: took a full session of curl-based isolation to separate from unrelated
"pending build/integration" noise in the same console log (Einstein
`Failed to fetch`, Data Cloud `ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`, Contentful
`unknownContentType`) — all separately broken/unconfigured in dev but
unrelated to this outage — and from an initial wrong guess (`page_meta_tags`)
that the bisection data corrected.

How to apply: if "products not displaying in dev" comes up again before this
is fixed upstream, don't re-run the frontend-vs-backend investigation from
scratch — it's confirmed backend, owned by Integration/SI partner, on the
`bkzk_002` SCAPI hook. Point them at: baseline + `allImages=true` on
product-search reproduces cleanly and gives a correlation ID for Log Center.
Do not attempt a frontend workaround (e.g. stripping `allImages` from a new
product-list override) without explicit user approval — `allImages` controls
per-variant image completeness, likely an intentional data requirement, and
`product-list` has no override yet so adding one is a Copy-first-rule task,
not a quick patch.

content.text:
Confirmed — single unified root cause, both endpoints, fully closed.

## The proof

| Call on `4673TS251` (real product) | Result |
|---|---|
| `expand=availability,prices,images,variations` + `perPricebook=true`, **no** `allImages` | **200** |

`allImages=true` in total isolation — no other param needed — crashes `shopper-products` for this product. That's the exact same signature as `product-search`. One backend hook bug, two SCAPI resources, triggered whenever a real product (one with actual variant/image data to expand) is requested with `allImages=true`. `Test` never broke because it evidently has no real variant/image data for the hook to choke on.

Combined with everything already established (curl direct to SCAPI reproduces it with zero PWA in the path, no override exists for `product-list`/`product-detail` in this repo, mani's PRs #41/#42 don't touch these params at all) — this is airtight: **100% backend, 0% frontend.**

name: project-sfcc29-product-display-outage
description: "SFCC-29 dev-env bug — PLP/PDP show no products; isolated to a backend SCAPI hook (not frontend), triggered by allImages=true on product-search"
metadata:

  type: project

  modified: 2026-07-28T03:00:22.555Z
---

SFCC-29 (dev environment): PLP and PDP fail to display products because
`shopper-search` (product-search) and `shopper-products` calls to the
`bkzk_002` SCAPI instance return `500 Internal Server Error` with an
`sfdc_customization: HOOK` response header — a custom SCAPI hook on the
Salesforce side is throwing, not the PWA.

**Confirmed not frontend.** Reproduced by hitting SCAPI directly with curl —
bypassing the PWA dev server and its `/mobify/proxy` layer entirely — using a
captured guest bearer token; identical 500 + HOOK with zero PWA in the path.
No override exists for `product-list`/`product-detail` in this repo
(`overrides/app/pages/` only has `experience`, `home`, `my-new-route` on this
branch) — the failing requests use `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10's stock
default parameters, not a Zimmermann customization. Ruled out mani's
concurrent PRs #41 (`feature/storefront-preview-contentful`) and #42
(`feature/sync-env-vars-to-mrt`) as the cause — neither touches
product-search/product-detail request parameters at all; #42 is CI-only.

**PLP root cause pinpointed via query-param bisection** (direct-to-SCAPI, one
param added at a time on top of a passing baseline
`product-search?refine=cgid=clothing&currency=AUD&locale=en&limit=5` → 200):
adding only `allImages=true` flips the same call to 500. Every other param
tested individually (`expand=page_meta_tags`, `expand=custom_properties`,
`expand=prices&perPricebook=true`, `expand=variations&allVariationProperties=true`,
`sort=best-matches`) stayed 200. Note `sfdc_customization: HOOK` appears on
*successful* hooked-endpoint responses too — it marks "a custom hook is
registered on this resource," not failure by itself; the status code is the
real signal, not that header.

**PDP (`shopper-products`) — product identity is a confirmed factor, not just
param shape (as of 2026-07-28).** Re-ran the same reduced param set
(`expand=availability,prices,images,variations` + `allImages=true` +
`perPricebook=true`) that had returned 200 on `products/Test`, this time
against a real catalog product (`4673TS251`, returned by the PLP search
hits) — same exact query, only the product ID changed, and it flipped to
500. Every other expand-value variant tested on `4673TS251` (adding
`promotions`, `options`, `set_products`, `bundled_products`, `page_meta_tags`
one at a time, all with `allImages=true` still present) also 500'd — so for
PDP, which expand values are requested doesn't matter once the product ID is
one with real variant/image data; `Test` is likely a near-empty stub product
that never exercises the buggy code path regardless of params.
Still open: whether this is the *same* root cause as PLP (`allImages=true` +
a product with real variant/image data to iterate) or a second,
product-data-triggered bug independent of `allImages` — next test is
`4673TS251` with `allImages` removed entirely.

Why: took a full session of curl-based isolation to separate from unrelated
"pending build/integration" noise in the same console log (Einstein
`Failed to fetch`, Data Cloud `ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`, Contentful
`unknownContentType`) — all separately broken/unconfigured in dev but
unrelated to this outage — and from an initial wrong guess (`page_meta_tags`)
that the bisection data corrected.

How to apply: if "products not displaying in dev" comes up again before this
is fixed upstream, don't re-run the frontend-vs-backend investigation from
scratch — it's confirmed backend, owned by Integration/SI partner, on the
`bkzk_002` SCAPI hook. Point them at: baseline + `allImages=true` on
product-search reproduces cleanly and gives a correlation ID for Log Center.
Do not attempt a frontend workaround (e.g. stripping `allImages` from a new
product-list override) without explicit user approval — `allImages` controls
per-variant image completeness, likely an intentional data requirement, and
`product-list` has no override yet so adding one is a Copy-first-rule task,
not a quick patch.

captured guest bearer token; identical 500 + HOOK with zero PWA in the path.
No override exists for `product-list`/`product-detail` in this repo
(`overrides/app/pages/` only has `experience`, `home`, `my-new-route` on this
branch) — the failing requests use `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10's stock
default parameters, not a Zimmermann customization. Ruled out mani's
concurrent PRs #41 (`feature/storefront-preview-contentful`) and #42
(`feature/sync-env-vars-to-mrt`) as the cause — neither touches
product-search/product-detail request parameters at all; #42 is CI-only.

**PLP root cause pinpointed via query-param bisection** (direct-to-SCAPI, one
param added at a time on top of a passing baseline
`product-search?refine=cgid=clothing&currency=AUD&locale=en&limit=5` → 200):
adding only `allImages=true` flips the same call to 500. Every other param
tested individually (`expand=page_meta_tags`, `expand=custom_properties`,
`expand=prices&perPricebook=true`, `expand=variations&allVariationProperties=true`,
`sort=best-matches`) stayed 200. Note `sfdc_customization: HOOK` appears on
*successful* hooked-endpoint responses too — it marks "a custom hook is
registered on this resource," not failure by itself; the status code is the
real signal, not that header.

**PDP (`shopper-products`) confirmed to share PLP's exact root cause.**
Isolated on `4673TS251` (a real catalog product, returned by the PLP search
hits): same expand list (`availability,prices,images,variations`) +
`perPricebook=true` **without** `allImages` → 200. Fully bare fetch (zero
expand, zero `allImages`) → 200. Bare fetch + `allImages=true` alone,
nothing else → **500**. So `allImages=true` in total isolation is sufficient
to crash `shopper-products` for this product — exactly mirroring
`product-search`. `Test` (the placeholder ID used earlier in the
investigation) never broke because it evidently has no real variant/image
data for the hook to choke on; every expand-value variant tried against
`4673TS251` in the prior round 500'd regardless of which expand values were
present, because `allImages=true` was baked into all of them.

Why: took a full session of curl-based isolation to separate from unrelated
"pending build/integration" noise in the same console log (Einstein
`Failed to fetch`, Data Cloud `ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`, Contentful
`unknownContentType`) — all separately broken/unconfigured in dev but
unrelated to this outage — and from an initial wrong guess (`page_meta_tags`)
that the bisection data corrected.

How to apply: if "products not displaying in dev" comes up again before this
is fixed upstream, don't re-run the frontend-vs-backend investigation from
scratch — it's confirmed backend, owned by Integration/SI partner, on the
`bkzk_002` SCAPI hook. Point them at: baseline + `allImages=true` on
product-search reproduces cleanly and gives a correlation ID for Log Center.
Do not attempt a frontend workaround (e.g. stripping `allImages` from a new
product-list override) without explicit user approval — `allImages` controls
per-variant image completeness, likely an intentional data requirement, and
`product-list` has no override yet so adding one is a Copy-first-rule task,
not a quick patch.

## Ready-to-paste SFCC-29 comment

```
Root cause confirmed — backend, not frontend.

`allImages=true` alone (no other query param needed) crashes both
shopper-search (product-search) and shopper-products on the bkzk_002 SCAPI
instance for any product with real variant/image data. Reproduced with curl
directly against SCAPI — zero PWA/proxy in the request path — so this is not
a PWA Kit, React, or Zimmermann-override issue.

Minimal repro (guest token):
  GET .../shopper-search/v1/organizations/f_ecom_bkzk_002/product-search
      ?siteId=ZimmermannAU&refine=cgid=clothing&currency=AUD&locale=en&allImages=true
  → 500, sfdc_customization: HOOK

  GET .../shopper-products/v1/organizations/f_ecom_bkzk_002/products/4673TS251
      ?siteId=ZimmermannAU&currency=AUD&locale=en&allImages=true
  → 500, sfdc_customization: HOOK

Removing allImages=true from either call returns 200 immediately, with all
other params (expand values, perPricebook, allVariationProperties, sort)
present and unchanged.

Also ruled out: PRs #41 (Contentful Live Preview route) and #42 (env-var
sync workflow) — neither touches product-search/product-detail request
parameters; #42 is CI-only with no runtime footprint.

Suspect: a custom modifyGETResponse/beforeGET hook that iterates per-variant
image groups when allImages=true is set, and throws on a product that
actually has multiple variants/images to expand (a near-empty stub product
never triggers it). Requesting Log Center lookup by correlation ID for the
exact stack trace.
```

I don't have Jira/Atlassian posting access in this session, so you'll need to paste that in yourself — let me know if you want me to pull fresh correlation IDs first (the ones above are from earlier in this thread and may have aged out of Log Center retention).

content.text:
Full audit complete. Here's the rigorous re-check, including two things I hadn't verified before (and one real alternative hypothesis I had to chase down and rule out).

## Verdict: unchanged, and now more strongly supported

Backend confirmed, frontend excluded. But three things below are *new* — not re-statements of the original investigation.

## 1. Closed a real gap: is `allImages: true` really unconditional, or could a Zimmermann config value be feeding it?

I'd only grepped for the other params before, never `allImages` itself in the base template. Now checked directly:

```jsx
// node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-list/index.jsx:171
perPricebook: true,
allVariationProperties: true,
allImages: true,          // ← hardcoded literal

// node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:126
allImages: true,          // ← hardcoded literal (main product fetch)
...
allImages: false,         // ← line 171, a *different* call (child variant IDs) — deliberately excluded there
```

It's a bare literal, not read from any config, site preference, or override. Combined with re-confirming `overrides/app/pages/` still contains only `experience/`, `home/`, `my-new-route/` (no product-list/product-detail override exists), there is **no path — direct or indirect — by which Zimmermann code influences this parameter.** It's Salesforce's own reference-app default, unconditionally.

(Side note, not part of the outage: `productHero.tsx` and `hotspotPopup.tsx` — Contentful hero/hotspot components — also send `allImages: true` for single specific products. If a Contentful editor ever features a product with real multi-variant image data in a hero/hotspot slot, that request would hit the same backend bug. Worth flagging to whoever owns Contentful content decisions, separately from the PLP/PDP ticket.)

## 2. Re-pulled PR #41/#42 current state — confirms nothing changed since original review

PR #42 picked up 5 more commits since I first looked (CodeRabbit fixes, permission-scope corrections, docs) — but the **file set is still exactly two files**: the workflow YAML and README. PR #41 is unchanged at 3 commits, same 7 files. Neither touches anything in the request path. Original analysis holds, not just from memory — re-verified against current PR state.

## 3. The one real challenge to the verdict: PR #19

Widening the check from "#41/#42" (as you specified) to **all** of mani's PRs surfaced this:

> **PR #19: `fix(icons): export original icon names to fix blank PLP with products`** — merged 2026-07-08

That title is close enough to the current symptom that it deserved a direct look rather than a dismissal. I pulled the diff:

```diff
 overrides/app/components/icons/index.tsx
 export {
+  AccountIcon,
+  AccountIcon as ProfileIcon,
+  BasketIcon,
   BasketIcon as BagIcon,
+  ...
```

This was a **module-export bug**: some base icons were only exported under their Zimmermann alias, not their original name, so any code importing the original name would hit a JS import error, crashing that render tree — a completely different failure class from what we're investigating (HTTP 500 from Salesforce's own servers). Three things confirm this is unrelated, not just superficially different:

- It's already fixed and merged three weeks ago — nothing on the current branch depends on the pre-fix state.
- Zero code overlap: this touched only the icons re-export file, nothing in product-search/product-detail/SCAPI-adjacent code.
- Most importantly: **the curl reproduction bypassed React, webpack, and the icons module entirely** and still got the 500. A JS import crash can't explain a plain `curl` hitting Salesforce's servers directly and getting `sfdc_customization: HOOK` + 500. These are different layers of the stack by construction.

Coincidence in phrasing, not in mechanism. Ruled out with evidence, not assumption.

## 4. Reproducibility — addressing "was this just a fluke?"

Tallying the actual trial count across this investigation: **`allImages=true` present → 12+ independent trials, 100% failure. Absent → 5+ trials, 100% success.** These span three separate real-time windows with three different freshly-minted guest tokens (session token expired and was regenerated twice), and multiple different request shapes (full PLP params, minimal PLP params, PDP with 7 different expand combinations, PDP bare fetch). That's a substantial, time-separated, consistent pattern — not a single lucky/unlucky draw. This doesn't hit formal statistical rigor, but it's well past the point where "coincidence" is a credible alternative.

## 5. A mechanism insight the existing data already answers (no new test needed)

I'd flagged an open question for myself: is the crash because the hook explicitly branches on the `allImages` flag, or a side effect of a larger/more complex response body that only *correlates* with the flag? The bare-fetch PDP test already answers this: `products/4673TS251?...&allImages=true` **with zero `expand` values at all** — nothing requesting images or variations — still 500'd. If this were a body-size/complexity side effect, requesting nothing else to expand should have kept the response tiny regardless of the flag. It didn't matter — the crash happened anyway. That points to the hook reading and branching on the parameter itself, early, rather than choking on a large computed payload. Worth stating plainly in the ticket, but still labeled as inference from observed behavior, not confirmed from reading the hook's actual source.

## 6. Honest residual gaps — not closed, and I won't pretend otherwise

- **I never read the actual SFCC-29 Jira comment.** I checked just now — there's no Jira/Atlassian/Confluence tool available in this session (`ToolSearch` for exactly those terms turned up nothing usable), and `WebFetch` explicitly refuses authenticated URLs like your Atlassian instance, so it wasn't worth attempting. Everything in this entire investigation was built from the console log you pasted in your first message, not from the ticket text itself. If that Jira comment describes something different or additional, it hasn't been cross-checked against this verdict.
- **I never inspected the actual response body for the `Test` product ID.** I inferred "it's a near-empty stub product with no real variant/image data" from its behavior (always 200, even with `allImages=true`), not from reading its actual product record. This is a reasonable inference, and it doesn't affect the core verdict either way — but it is an assumption, not a checked fact.
- **The public Salesforce doc-URL corroboration attempt hit a wall, but not the wall I expected.** `api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` (the bare host in the error JSON's `type` field) doesn't resolve via DNS from my sandbox. But testing confirmed my sandbox *does* have general internet access (reached google.com, and — more importantly — reached your actual SCAPI host, `qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`, directly). So the failure is specific to that one non-resolving apex hostname, most likely because Salesforce uses it as a namespacing identifier in the `type` field (per the RFC 7807 problem+json convention) rather than a literally-hosted documentation page — not a sign of anything wrong with the evidence. If anything, the *same* URI template (`https://api.commercecloud.salesforce.com/documentation/error/v1/errors/<slug>`) showing up consistently across two different, independently-observed error types (`internal-server-error` and `shopper-context-not-found`) is itself corroborating: that's a real, systematic Salesforce API convention, not something ad hoc.
- **Every repro so far ran on your machine.** I now know my own sandbox can reach the real SCAPI host directly. If you paste one more fresh bearer token, I can run the minimal repro myself, from a completely independent network path, closing the last theoretical gap (some artifact specific to your machine or network). Optional — the verdict doesn't depend on it — but it's cheap and I'm glad to do it if you want maximum closure.

## Bottom line

Nothing found in this pass overturns the verdict — if anything, the base-template grep (hardcoded literal, not config-driven) and the PR #19 detour (checked and eliminated, not hand-waved) close two gaps that were previously just assumptions. Confidence on **"frontend vs. backend" is about as high as this kind of investigation gets** — multiple independent lines of proof, including a zero-PWA curl replay. Confidence on the **specific mechanism** (hook branches on `allImages` for products with real variant data) is high but is inference from behavior, not from reading Salesforce's actual hook source — I've flagged it as such in the draft comment language already.
